question: Should Testbox lease freshness promise only a best-effort timeout for killable Git children, or must it reliably escape the stale-filesystem scenario described in the PR?
rationale: The current synchronous Node boundary can prove the first behavior with the supplied shim, but the second needs a different mechanism or direct evidence; selecting the product/operational guarantee is maintainer intent.

options.title: Narrow to killable-child timeout
options.body: Keep the helper timeout, revise the claim and proof to cover only Git children that respond to `SIGKILL`, and document that it is not a stale-filesystem hard deadline.

options.title: Require a supervisory boundary
options.body: Pause this patch and design a workflow or runner-level watchdog that can provide a real deadline for the stale-filesystem failure mode.

recommendation.title: Narrow to killable-child timeout
recommendation.body: Keep the helper timeout, revise the claim and proof to cover only Git children that respond to `SIGKILL`, and document that it is not a stale-filesystem hard deadline.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged timeout work is the closest repository precedent for deciding the intended automation boundary.
